6. Post-exploitation: Once the hacker has gained access to the system, they will attempt to escalate their privileges and gain access to sensitive data or systems.
7. Reporting: Finally, the hacker will document their findings and provide a report to the system owner, detailing the vulnerabilities that were identified and the recommended countermeasures.

Some common tools used in ethical hacking include Nmap, Metasploit, and Wireshark. It is important to note that ethical hacking should only be performed with the consent of the system owner and in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

In summary, ethical hacking involves testing a system's security to identify vulnerabilities and recommend countermeasures.
